messages.author: 67571e909b2d8a9a
messages.subject: Help required for 'read.transcript.features' function
parts:
Hi,
 
Could I please get some advise using the 'read.transcript.features' function? I downloaded my annotation 'refFlat' and 'refGene' from the UCSC genome browser using the table browser. When I uploaded the latter annotation 'refGene', using the  'read.transcript.features' function, it works fine. In contrast, when I uploaded the  'refFlat'  file using  'read.transcript.features' function, it came up with the following error:
 
Error in .Call2("solve_user_SEW0", start, end, width, PACKAGE = "IRanges") : 
  solving row 13: negative widths are not allowed

 

I am not sure what this error means but I had a look at row 13 an it is blank so I am not sure what is this error all about. I would like to use the 'refFlat' file for annotation as it contains the gene name as oppose to transcript_id.
 
Could someone please advice how I may resolve this issue?
 
Many thanks.

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Help required for 'read.transcript.features' function
parts:
Hi,

the methylKit function 'read.transcript.features' needs a bed formatted file with certain number of columns. Details about the bed file format needed for this function were explained previously in this forum (here is the thread).

Kindly check if your input file is of the same format (refFlat could be downloaded in multiple ways. If you want refFlat as input for methylKit it need to be in bed format).

For a quick and sharp solution, you may share few lines of your input file format and details of how the function is used (Well, its difficult to understand what is the issue with the limited details provided in the mail)!


Regards,
Kalyan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Help required for 'read.transcript.features' function
parts:
the problem here is that refFlat file have the same transcript name (in this case gene name) for multiple transcripts. methylKit would deal with that if the transcripts having the same ids are mapping to different locations, some refseq transcripts are like that in some species.

my suggestion is to use unique transcript ids in bed files. refseq and ensembl downloads would normally produce such files. IF you can't generate bed files with unique identifiers pick one of the transcript as the canonical transcript or make the identifiers unique by adding things like "_1", something that you can remove with regular expression later on.  

If you use refseq or ensemble tables and  you need gene symbols to transcript id mappings, you can always get that from annotation packages at bioconductor, or download the mapping table from UCSC or via rtracklayer. 

Best,
Altuna
